name: Elite U.S. Legal & Commercial Correspondence Playbook
purpose: Encode the functional logic behind high-stakes U.S. legal, executive and international-project correspondence without copying any named lawyer's personal prose or inventing legal authority.

core_interpretation.explanation: The 'insider' quality is usually compressed professional signaling: what is a fact, what is the present position, what is conditional, what is being preserved, what decision is requested, and what happens next. Treat these as functional signals, not magical phrases.
core_interpretation.priority: substance and record control before style

signals.function: Put the decision, recommendation or requested action before background so a senior reader can act immediately.
signals.test: The first substantive paragraph tells the reader what position/action matters.

signals.function: Anchor assertions to dates, documents, matter/project references and contemporaneous records rather than adjectives or reconstructed memory.
signals.test: Every material factual proposition can be traced to a supplied record or is marked for verification.

signals.function: Tie the position to verified contract text, law, precedent, policy or an approved institutional playbook.
signals.test: No clause, case, statute or policy is cited unless supplied or independently verified.

signals.function: Make the commitment state legible: inquiry, proposal, present position, conditional willingness, firm instruction or final commitment.
examples: We would be prepared to consider… provided that…
signals.warning: Do not use conditional wording to disguise a commitment the user actually intends to make.

signals.function: State dependencies explicitly so silence, sequence or courtesy language does not accidentally become consent.
signals.test: Conditions and reciprocal steps are expressed next to the corresponding proposal.

signals.function: Show who owns the next decision, information gap, cost, timing risk or approval without unnecessary accusation.
signals.test: The letter identifies the operational consequence and the responsible next action.

signals.function: Choose a posture deliberately: cooperative clarification, executive decision request, formal notice, reservation, dispute position or settlement communication.
signals.test: Tone and legal effect match the selected posture; a routine email is not silently converted into a formal notice.

signals.function: End with one clear ask, owner, deadline or next procedural step.
signals.test: The recipient can answer 'what do you want me to do, and by when?' from the closing paragraph alone.

signals.function: Use professional terminology where it carries legal/project meaning, but remove jargon that only performs status.
signals.test: Every technical or legal term changes meaning, scope, proof or procedure.

sequence: two-to-five record facts that control the decision
only the rights reservation actually supported by verified law/contract
dispute-preservation.tone: firm without gratuitous hostility; evidentiary rather than emotional

sequence: position or purpose of the letter

context_dependent_labels.rule: Never insert these merely because they sound sophisticated. Enable only when the user confirms the factual/legal basis or the applicable jurisdiction/contract has been verified. A label never substitutes for a required contractual notice, addressee, delivery method or time bar.

notice_controls: verify who must receive the notice
verify permitted delivery method and deemed-receipt mechanics
preserve contemporaneous programme, cost, instruction and site records
separate request for instruction from assertion of entitlement

quality_gates: No invented fact, date, quote, case, statute, clause, precedent or approval.
No context-dependent legal label without a confirmed basis.
No stylistic flourish that changes the legal/commercial commitment accidentally.
No vague close: the requested action and next step must be explicit.
No formal-notice claim unless the required contract/jurisdiction mechanics were verified.
Distinguish evidence, inference, legal conclusion and commercial recommendation.

reference_sources.title: Tips for Writing Effective Emails to Your Clients
reference_sources.portable_lesson: Lead with important information, stay focused, state recommendations and next steps/deadlines.

reference_sources.title: Professional Email Communication
reference_sources.portable_lesson: Professional email should be brief, direct, reader-centered and appropriately formal.

reference_sources.title: Construction Claims & Responses
reference_sources.portable_lesson: Persuasive construction claims follow a logical contract/cause/effect/entitlement/quantum structure and rely on records.

reference_sources.title: FIDIC Contracts Guide / FAQ material on notices and claims
reference_sources.portable_lesson: Notice wording, timing and contemporaneous records are procedural evidence, not decorative formalism.
